purpose: Measure whether event transport health accounts for every attempted sequence, including losses at the final stream boundary, before an observer claims loss-free process evidence.

comparison_arms.description: BPF ring buffer with aggregate counters but no pre-publication sequence allocation or terminal high-water fence.
BPF ring buffer with per-source/partition attempted sequence numbers allocated before reservation, classified loss ranges and terminal close fence.
Linux perf-buffer transport with native lost-sample callbacks and the same task workload.
Pinned Falco modern eBPF version/configuration with metrics explicitly enabled and native scap drop counters retained without double counting.
Pinned Tetragon process lifecycle event and export path with available health/queue metrics captured.
ptrace/wait lifecycle event capture with tracer stop/continue overhead and its exact task-level scope disclosed.
Controlled transport deliberately drops selected sequences and serves as a positive control for loss detection.

metrics.definition: Fraction of attempted source-epoch sequence numbers accounted exactly once as published, lost, required-discarded or explicitly excluded.
Fraction of independently injected loss events/ranges detected by sequence or explicit source counters and prevented from a loss-free claim.
Count of source epochs accepted loss-free despite seeded loss, unclassified sequence holes, counter inconsistency, missing close fences, restarts or unmonitored producers.
Fraction of source epochs whose published/lost/discard counts exactly match counts derived from event records and classified ranges.
Fraction of final-attempted-sequence losses detected when no later event exists to expose an ordinary interior sequence gap.
Fraction of required-event discards explicitly classified and denied loss-free promotion; excluded policy suppressions remain separately visible.
Fraction of source epochs with producer quiescence, terminal fence, consumer drain acknowledgement and no unmonitored producers or restart.
95th-percentile hook-to-consumer publication latency on the declared event-size and event-rate workload.
95th-percentile workload slowdown relative to the same task without event capture.

gates.promotion_rule: Every safety gate is non-compensatory. Efficiency is evaluated only after all safety gates pass. A composite score may not compensate for unclassified sequence loss.

statistical_protocol.clustering: Events, sequence numbers, retries and repeated fault injections within one source epoch are not independent samples.
statistical_protocol.splits: Development, qualification and untouched confirmatory source configurations/task lineages are separated. Do not randomize individual events across splits.
statistical_protocol.stopping: Preregister source/host counts, kernel strata, buffer capacities, fault schedules, event rates, retries, exclusions and confidence intervals before qualification.
